source_facts.fact: The ENEO-hosted ARSEL decision states that medium-voltage pricing has a 3,700 XAF/kW monthly fixed subscribed-power charge plus a time/use-dependent proportional charge.
source_facts.quotation_or_reference: Decision 0096/ARSEL/DG/DCEC/SDCT, Article 1, II: 'une prime fixe mensuelle de 3700FCFA par kW de puissance souscrite' and general regime <1 MW energy rates: 70 XAF/kWh for 23:00–18:00 and 85 XAF/kWh for 18:00–23:00 at 0–200 hours. The decision is dated 28 May 2012 and effective 1 June 2012; ENEO still publishes it as its tariff page as of the research date.

source_facts.fact: The same decision labels tariffs as tax-exclusive and preserves VAT exemption only for electricity consumption at or below 110 kWh.
source_facts.quotation_or_reference: Article 1: 'tarifs de vente hors taxes'; Article 2 preserves VAT exemption for 'consommations d’électricité inférieures ou égales à 110 kWh'.

modeling.assumption: Charging scheduled primarily in the ENEO 23:00–18:00 period and within the 0–200 monthly utilization-hours band; connected load below 1 MW.
modeling.candidate_tax_treatment: Tax-exclusive. VAT is normally an input tax for a registered business and is not added to the model row. If VAT is nonrecoverable, gross energy-only cash cost is 70 * 1.1925 / 573.714 = 0.145499 USD/kWh.
modeling.fixed_and_demand_charges: The 3,700 XAF/kW-month subscribed-power charge is excluded because no charger contracted-kW and monthly-kWh profile was supplied. Effective all-in USD/kWh must add (3,700 * subscribed_kW / monthly_kWh) / 573.714, plus nonrecoverable tax if applicable.
other_sensitivities: Charging during 18:00–23:00 uses 85 XAF/kWh = 0.148157 USD/kWh tax-exclusive, or 0.176678 USD/kWh with nonrecoverable VAT.

If the site is instead eligible for low-voltage non-residential service, the published top cited band is 99 XAF/kWh = 0.172560 USD/kWh tax-exclusive, or 0.205778 USD/kWh with nonrecoverable VAT. This was not selected because a vessel charger is more plausibly medium voltage.
exclusions: Power-factor, reactive-energy, outage/back-up generation, and site-specific levies not evidenced in the cited tariff

historical_concession_canon.source_vintage: ARESEP resolution RRG-8666-2008, tariff projection for 2009 and 2010

They are stale, operator-level rather than demonstrably per-vessel, and the decision does not establish that they are berth/terminal charges. They are not used or inflation-scaled.

marina_and_marine_administration.registration_fact: Registro Nacional publishes vessel registration charges based on contractual/fiscal value plus stamps and a Guardacostas registration right. Ley 8000 Article 33 sets that Guardacostas registration right at 5%, 10%, or 15% of the statutory salary base by length. Registration is a one-time event, vessel value is unknown, and no annualization life is supplied, so it is excluded from the annual candidate.
why_complete_value_still_not_modeled: No current MOPT/operator/terminal tariff or concession document was found that states berth, ramp, terminal-use, or route-concession payment for a new vessel on either route.
The current annual certificate canon is length-based, but candidate vessel length is unspecified.

The 2008 ARESEP concession-canon values are stale, were projections from a study then awaiting approval, and are operator-level; silently indexing or dividing them by historical fleet count would violate the evidence rule.
State ownership of the terminals does not prove that terminal use is free.
Registration charges are event-based and partly vessel-value-based, not annual operating fees.
Generic marina or Caldera commercial-port tariffs are not comparable to these MOPT public cabotage terminals.
Insurance and charging infrastructure remain excluded by definition.
